themes.thesis: Capex supercycle still compounding; the bottleneck the whole AI economy pays a toll to.
Electricity is the binding constraint on AI. Multi-decade buildout, but 2026 prices already discount a lot.
Structural rearmament plus a genuine software/autonomy displacement of primes.
The next frontier after language models, but revenue is still mostly ahead of the narrative.
Storage attach rates and supply-chain onshoring are policy-supported and accelerating.
Launch cost collapse is real; direct-to-device is the swing factor. High dispersion, high beta.
Stablecoin rails are a real threat to card economics — this theme has a genuine short side.
Obesity franchise economics are extraordinary; AI-discovery pure plays remain unproven.
Biggest winners are the hyperscalers; seat-based SaaS faces the clearest AI business-model risk.
Non-discretionary spend, but AI is compressing seat-based pricing and inviting autonomous-agent entrants.

privates.name: OpenAI
privates.description: Leading AI lab (ChatGPT, GPT models) whose massive compute purchasing and custom silicon ambitions reshape chip demand
privates.threat: OpenAI's push for custom inference silicon (with Broadcom) and alternative chip suppliers (Cerebras, AMD) threatens to diversify demand away from pure Nvidia dependence while its scale validates the entire AI-chip buildout.

privates.name: Anthropic
privates.description: AI safety-focused lab (Claude models) with massive multi-cloud compute commitments across chip vendors
privates.threat: Anthropic's diversified compute strategy across AWS Trainium, Google TPUs, and Nvidia GPUs pressures Nvidia's pricing power and validates alternative accelerator architectures at hyperscale.

privates.name: xAI
privates.description: Elon Musk's AI lab (Grok models) building some of the world's largest GPU clusters (Colossus)
privates.threat: xAI's rapid buildout of the largest GPU clusters in the world is one of Nvidia's single biggest demand drivers, while its interest in alternative silicon signals future diversification risk.

privates.name: Cerebras Systems
privates.description: Maker of wafer-scale AI chips (WSE-3) for ultra-fast inference, now publicly traded after May 2026 IPO
privates.threat: Cerebras's wafer-scale architecture beat Nvidia on single-user inference speed and landed a $10B OpenAI compute deal, proving non-GPU inference architectures can win at hyperscale before Cerebras itself went public.

privates.name: Groq
privates.description: Inference-chip pioneer (LPU) pivoting to an inference-cloud operator after licensing its core IP to Nvidia
privates.threat: Nvidia's reported $20B non-exclusive licensing deal for Groq's LPU technology both validates fast-inference architecture as a real threat and shows Nvidia absorbing rather than losing to non-GPU challengers.

privates.name: SambaNova Systems
privates.description: AI chipmaker (SN40L/SN50) focused on inference chips and on-premise enterprise AI deployments
privates.threat: SambaNova's on-premise inference chips and near-acquisition talks with Intel highlight both real enterprise demand for Nvidia alternatives and the difficulty of independently scaling against Nvidia's ecosystem lock-in.

privates.name: Tenstorrent
privates.description: Jim Keller-led AI chip designer building discrete, workstation-scale AI accelerators, reportedly in acquisition talks with Qualcomm
privates.last_round: Reported $8-10B acquisition talks with Qualcomm, Jul 2026 (prior: sought $3.2B valuation round, Nov 2025)
privates.threat: Qualcomm's reported bid for Tenstorrent at up to $10B signals large semiconductor incumbents see standalone AI-chip IP as strategically necessary, validating the broader non-Nvidia accelerator thesis.

privates.name: Etched
privates.description: Builder of transformer-specific ASICs (Sohu chip) designed exclusively to accelerate transformer-model inference
privates.threat: Etched's bet that a transformer-only ASIC can dramatically outperform general-purpose GPUs on cost-per-token is a direct wager against Nvidia's flexible-architecture moat.

privates.name: Fermi America
privates.description: Developer of the world's largest private, behind-the-meter nuclear-and-gas power grid and AI data-center campus in Texas
privates.threat: Fermi's plan to build a private, off-grid multi-gigawatt power campus (nuclear, gas, solar, storage) competing directly for hyperscaler tenants threatens to disintermediate incumbent regulated utilities and IPPs from AI power contracts.

privates.name: Valar Atomics
privates.description: Developer of standardized, mass-manufactured waterless small modular nuclear reactors for AI data centers
privates.threat: Valar's factory-built waterless reactors, already powering an Nvidia Blackwell cluster in partnership with Nvidia, threaten to undercut incumbent generators on speed-to-power for AI campuses.

privates.name: Blue Energy Global
privates.description: Startup building grid-scale nuclear reactors constructed in shipyards to cut cost and schedule for data-center power
privates.threat: Blue Energy's shipyard-manufacturing model for 1.5GW reactors targets the same speed-to-power gap that has driven utilities and IPPs to underbuild for AI demand, offering a faster alternative supply route.

privates.name: Antares Nuclear
privates.description: Small modular reactor developer targeting U.S. military bases and price-insensitive critical infrastructure customers
privates.threat: Antares's Pentagon-backed SMR contracts show private nuclear capital increasingly bypassing traditional utility procurement, creating an alternative power-supply track for critical AI and defense loads.

privates.name: Crusoe Energy
privates.description: Vertically integrated 'AI factory' company combining rapid energy sourcing, data-center construction, and cloud services (developer behind Stargate Abilene)
privates.last_round: $1.375B Series E (equity, Oct 2025) plus $11.6B debt/equity phase-two (May 2026)
privates.total_raised: $3B+ equity, plus tens of billions in project debt
privates.threat: Crusoe's model of bundling power sourcing with data-center construction lets hyperscalers skip traditional utility interconnection queues, threatening to route gigawatts of new demand around incumbent grid operators and IPPs.

privates.name: CoreWeave
privates.description: GPU-cloud operator whose massive power procurement and financing structures underpin the AI-infrastructure debt market (note: now publicly traded, included for power-market relevance)
privates.stage: publicly traded (IPO Mar 2025), power/financing model still disrupting sector
privates.threat: CoreWeave's GPU-backed, investment-grade financing structure lets it lock up 1.7GW of active power capacity via bankruptcy-remote SPVs, a template competitors and IPPs must now match to win hyperscaler leases.

privates.name: Vantage Data Centers
privates.description: Private data-center developer building multi-gigawatt AI campuses (Stargate Frontier, Lighthouse) financed via infrastructure debt
privates.last_round: $25B Frontier campus commitment, 2026 (project financing, not corporate equity round)
privates.total_raised: tens of billions in project-level debt and equity since 2020
privates.threat: Vantage's ability to finance and deliver 1,000+ MW campuses within a single year outpaces the buildout cadence of regulated utilities, forcing incumbents to accelerate capacity additions or lose hyperscaler tenants.

privates.name: TerraPower
privates.description: Bill Gates-backed developer of next-generation Natrium sodium-fast nuclear reactors for industrial and tech customers
privates.last_round: Undisclosed growth funding, ongoing (DOE-backed demonstration project in Wyoming)
privates.threat: TerraPower's advanced Natrium reactor, backed by Amazon and Bill Gates, positions next-gen nuclear as a long-horizon threat to gas-peaker and traditional nuclear operators competing for AI baseload contracts.

privates.name: Anduril Industries
privates.description: Vertically integrated defense company building autonomous drones, munitions, and software (Lattice OS) for the US military and allies
privates.threat: Anduril's software-defined, mass-manufactured autonomy platforms directly threaten legacy primes' cost-plus hardware model while validating investor appetite for defense disruption at massive scale.

privates.name: Shield AI
privates.description: Maker of Hivemind autonomy software and X-Bat autonomous aircraft for contested-environment drone operations
privates.threat: Selection for the US Air Force Collaborative Combat Aircraft program shows autonomy software startups can win prime roles on next-gen fighter drone programs traditionally reserved for LMT/RTX.

privates.name: Saronic Technologies
privates.description: Builder of autonomous surface vessels (Marauder-class) for naval defense and maritime autonomy at scale
privates.threat: Saronic's rapid unmanned-vessel production (targeting 20+ ships/year) directly challenges traditional shipbuilders and primes for Navy uncrewed surface vessel programs at a fraction of legacy cost and schedule.

privates.name: Helsing
privates.description: Munich-based European defense AI company building software for drones, aircraft, and submarines for NATO militaries
privates.threat: As Europe's largest defense startup pushing 'sovereign AI,' Helsing threatens US primes' access to European rearmament budgets and validates AI-native defense software as a category outside the US market.

privates.name: Epirus
privates.description: Maker of Leonidas high-power microwave counter-drone directed-energy weapon systems
privates.threat: Epirus' directed-energy counter-swarm systems offer a cheaper, scalable alternative to missile-based air defense sold by RTX and LMT, addressing the drone-saturation threat exposed in recent conflicts.

privates.name: Castelion
privates.description: SpaceX-alumni-founded startup mass-producing low-cost hypersonic strike weapons (Blackbeard)
privates.threat: Castelion's commercial-style rapid iteration on hypersonic munitions challenges LMT/RTX's historic monopoly on hypersonic weapons development and could undercut their unit economics on future contracts.

privates.name: Applied Intuition
privates.description: Vehicle intelligence/simulation software company expanding into defense autonomy (Axion, Acuity) via EpiSci acquisition
privates.threat: Applied Intuition's push from autonomous-vehicle simulation into defense autonomy software threatens to displace prime-built mission software and simulation environments used across LMT/RTX programs.

privates.name: Skydio
privates.description: US-made autonomous drone manufacturer serving enterprise, public safety, and defense customers, positioned against DJI
privates.threat: Skydio's domestic manufacturing scale and regulatory tailwinds from Chinese-drone bans directly erode AeroVironment's small-drone market share in public safety and defense.

privates.name: SpaceX
privates.description: Dominant launch, Starlink satellite broadband, and Starship deep-space company preparing for a landmark IPO
privates.threat: SpaceX's Starlink and Starship dominance dwarfs every public space comp combined, and its pending IPO (targeting up to $800B+ valuation) will reset the entire sector's valuation benchmarks overnight.

privates.name: Stoke Space
privates.description: Developer of the fully and rapidly reusable Nova medium-lift launch vehicle at Cape Canaveral
privates.last_round: $860M Series D, Feb 2026 (in process of raising ~$1B further, Aug 2026)
privates.threat: Stoke's fully reusable Nova rocket, backed by a rising ~$9B valuation, directly targets Rocket Lab's and legacy primes' medium-lift launch market with a SpaceX-style reusability model.

privates.name: K2 Space
privates.description: Manufacturer of large, high-power satellite buses for commercial and defense constellations
privates.threat: K2's high-power large-satellite platforms compete directly with Iridium's and AST SpaceMobile's next-gen constellation hardware, and its rapid production model threatens legacy satellite bus suppliers.

privates.name: True Anomaly
privates.description: Builder of autonomous spacecraft and space-based interceptors for space domain awareness and Golden Dome missile defense
privates.threat: True Anomaly's space-interceptor role in the Golden Dome missile-defense program positions it to capture national security space budgets that would otherwise flow to Boeing and legacy space-defense primes.

privates.name: Impulse Space
privates.description: Builder of orbital transfer vehicles ('space tugs') for in-space mobility, founded by SpaceX propulsion veteran Tom Mueller
privates.threat: Impulse Space's orbital mobility infrastructure threatens to become the default 'last mile' layer for satellite deployment, disintermediating launch providers like Rocket Lab from higher-margin orbit-raising services.

privates.name: Apex Space
privates.description: Mass-manufacturer of productized, configurable satellite bus platforms (Aries, Nova, Comet) for commercial and defense payloads
privates.threat: Apex's high-rate, standardized satellite bus production model undercuts custom-built satellite platforms, threatening incumbent suppliers' margins as Pentagon demand for rapid constellation deployment grows.

privates.name: Varda Space Industries
privates.description: Operator of reentry capsules for microgravity manufacturing (pharmaceuticals) and hypersonics testing
privates.threat: Varda's reentry-capsule and in-space manufacturing niche opens a new commercial space revenue category (pharma manufacturing, hypersonics testing) that diversifies demand beyond launch, indirectly pressuring Rocket Lab's reentry ambitions.

privates.name: Axiom Space
privates.description: Developer of commercial space station (Axiom Station) and NASA spacesuits (AxEMU) as ISS successor
privates.threat: Axiom's role as the leading ISS-successor commercial station builder directly challenges Boeing's legacy human-spaceflight infrastructure position as NASA transitions off the ISS by 2030.

privates.name: Figure AI
privates.description: Developer of general-purpose humanoid robots (Figure 03) for logistics, manufacturing and eventually home use
privates.threat: At a $39B valuation and backed by Nvidia and Brookfield, Figure directly threatens to leapfrog traditional industrial automation and warehouse robotics incumbents with general-purpose humanoids.

privates.name: Physical Intelligence
privates.description: Builds general-purpose AI foundation models ('robot brains') that can control many different robot bodies
privates.last_round: $600M, Nov 2025 (in talks for ~$1B more at >$11B, Mar 2026)
privates.threat: Its foundation-model 'brain' approach could commoditize the control software layer that industrial automation vendors like Rockwell and Fanuc currently bundle with their hardware.

privates.name: Skild AI
privates.description: Builds an 'omni-bodied' foundation model (Skild Brain) designed to operate any robot for any task across industrial and commercial settings
privates.threat: Skild's revenue-generating omni-bodied brain, already deployed in warehouses, manufacturing and data centers, threatens to displace proprietary robot-control software sold by industrial automation incumbents.

privates.name: Apptronik
privates.description: Austin-based maker of the Apollo humanoid robot for factories, warehouses and logistics, partnered with Google DeepMind
privates.threat: Apollo is already piloting in Mercedes-Benz and GXO Logistics facilities, positioning Apptronik to beat Tesla Optimus and Chinese humanoids to commercial warehouse/factory deployment ahead of incumbents like Rockwell and Symbotic.

privates.name: 1X Technologies
privates.description: Norwegian, OpenAI-backed maker of the NEO bipedal humanoid robot targeting home and enterprise (logistics, guarding) use
privates.threat: 1X's consumer-home NEO strategy, backed directly by OpenAI, opens an entirely new physical-AI market beyond industrial floors that none of the public comps currently address.

privates.name: Agility Robotics
privates.description: Maker of the Digit bipedal warehouse/logistics humanoid robot, going public via SPAC merger with Churchill Capital Corp XI
privates.threat: As the first pure-play humanoid robotics company to go public, Agility validates warehouse-humanoid economics deployed at Amazon, Toyota and GXO sites, directly threatening Symbotic and Zebra's warehouse automation stacks.

privates.name: Neura Robotics
privates.description: German full-stack cognitive robotics company building humanoid (4NE1) and industrial robots plus the Neuraverse shared-intelligence platform
privates.threat: Backed by major tech and industrial investors, Neura is Europe's best-funded physical-AI challenger to Fanuc- and Rockwell-style industrial automation incumbents.

privates.name: Unitree Robotics
privates.description: Hangzhou-based maker of humanoid robots and quadruped robot dogs, mainland China's first listed humanoid-robot company
privates.total_raised: IPO plus prior VC rounds from Geely, Alibaba, Tencent
privates.threat: Unitree's profitable, low-cost humanoid production model and fresh public capital threaten to undercut Western and Japanese robotics incumbents on price at scale.

privates.name: XBOW
privates.description: Autonomous offensive security platform that uses AI to discover and validate software vulnerabilities at scale, replacing manual penetration testing.
privates.threat: Autonomous AI pentesting commoditizes a core revenue stream for traditional MDR/EDR vendors and reduces dependence on human red teams that CRWD and PANW rely on as high-margin services.

privates.name: Socket
privates.description: Software supply chain security platform that protects enterprises from malicious open-source dependencies introduced via AI-assisted coding.
privates.threat: Addresses the fastest-growing attack surface in enterprise security — AI-generated code pulling in unvetted open-source packages — where CRWD and ZS lack native depth.

privates.name: Torq
privates.description: Agentic AI security operations platform automating SOC workflows, alert triage, and incident response for multinational enterprises.
privates.threat: Agentic SOC automation threatens the professional-services and Cortex XSOAR revenues of PANW and the Singularity suite upsell economics of SentinelOne.

privates.name: Abnormal AI
privates.description: AI-native email and collaboration security platform using behavioral analysis to stop sophisticated phishing, BEC, and account-takeover attacks.
privates.threat: Behavioral AI email security erodes email gateway revenues at PANW and CRWD and competes directly with OKTA's identity-centric threat detection as BEC attacks evolve.

privates.name: Zafran Security
privates.description: AI-native threat exposure management platform that uses existing security tools to prove 90% of critical vulnerabilities are unexploitable and autonomously remediates the remaining 10%.
privates.threat: Directly challenges vulnerability management modules in PANW's Cortex and CRWD's Falcon by reducing remediation times from weeks to hours using AI-native exposure scoring.

privates.name: Zenity
privates.description: Cybersecurity platform that governs and secures autonomous AI agents across enterprise environments, preventing agent-level attacks and data exfiltration.
privates.threat: As enterprises deploy millions of AI agents, Zenity's AI-agent governance layer fills a gap that CRWD, OKTA, and ZS have not yet addressed natively, threatening to become the de facto control plane for agentic security.

privates.name: Eye Security
privates.description: European integrated cybersecurity platform combining AI-powered threat detection, 24/7 human SOC, incident response, and in-house cyber insurance for mid-market enterprises.
privates.threat: Challenges FTNT and PANW's European mid-market position by offering a sovereign, GDPR-compliant integrated stack — particularly relevant as NIS2 drives mandatory security spend.

privates.name: Isomorphic Labs
privates.description: Alphabet-spun AI drug design company using AlphaFold-derived models to design novel therapeutics across multiple modalities, with partnerships with Lilly, Novartis, and J&J.
privates.threat: If IsoDDE delivers clinical candidates at scale, Isomorphic becomes a platform layer that renders traditional CRO-based discovery at LLY and NVO obsolete and could capture royalties on drug programs at both companies.

privates.name: Chai Discovery
privates.description: AI molecular design company building foundation models that predict and reprogram molecular interactions for drug discovery, with pharma partnerships with Lilly, Pfizer, and Novartis.
privates.threat: Chai-3's double-digit experimental success rate in de novo antibody design directly erodes SDGR's computational chemistry and RXRX's phenomics edge while commoditizing early discovery for big pharma partners LLY and NVO.

privates.name: Xaira Therapeutics
privates.description: Integrated AI biotech using generative protein design and large biological models to discover next-generation therapeutics targeting hard-to-drug biology.
privates.threat: With the deepest capital base in AI-native drug discovery and Nobel laureate co-founder David Baker, Xaira threatens to bypass clinical-stage public biotechs like VRTX by generating first-in-class biologics that legacy platforms cannot reach.

privates.name: EvolutionaryScale
privates.description: AI protein language model company (ESM3) that generates novel proteins compressing millions of years of evolution, enabling therapeutic and industrial biotech applications.
privates.threat: ESM3's open and commercial protein generation platform challenges ILMN's sequencing-centric data moat and SDGR's structural biology software by making de novo protein design accessible and cheap.

privates.name: insitro
privates.description: AI drug discovery company founded by Daphne Koller building a data engine around human biology with partnerships with BMS (ALS), Gilead (NASH), and Lilly (metabolism).
privates.threat: insitro's Virtual Human platform competing on ALS, NASH, and metabolic targets with BMS and Lilly validation undermines the narrative that public TechBio companies like RXRX have a monopoly on AI-native discovery.

privates.name: Genesis Therapeutics
privates.description: AI-native drug discovery company focused on generative chemistry and translational biology to produce clinical-stage small molecules for undruggable targets.
privates.threat: Genesis's generative chemistry platform directly competes with SDGR's Maestro and RXRX's Recursion OS by targeting the same undruggable protein space, threatening to make SDGR's software licensing model irrelevant.

privates.name: Form Energy
privates.description: Long-duration iron-air battery company capable of 100-hour discharge, targeting multi-day grid storage to complement intermittent renewables and AI data center power needs.
privates.threat: Iron-air chemistry with 10x lower cost per kWh than lithium threatens FLNC's and EOSE's long-duration propositions and could undercut TSLA's Megapack pricing for utility-scale deployments.

privates.name: Redwood Materials
privates.description: Battery recycling and cathode production company founded by ex-Tesla CTO JB Straubel, now expanding into second-life EV battery energy storage for AI data centers.
privates.threat: Redwood's recycling-to-cathode loop threatens ALB and MP by creating a domestic circular supply chain that reduces dependence on virgin lithium and rare earth imports, potentially capping long-term lithium pricing power.

privates.name: Base Power
privates.description: Residential and commercial energy storage company offering a 39.2 kWh home battery (Core) with 36-hour backup, deploying as a virtual power plant network.
privates.threat: Base Power's $13B valuation and VPP network model directly challenges ENPH's IQ Battery dominance and TSLA's Powerwall by offering longer backup duration and a utility-facing fleet monetization layer.

privates.name: Sila Nanotechnologies
privates.description: Battery materials startup producing silicon-carbon anode material that increases energy density for EVs and grid storage, with manufacturing in Moses Lake, WA.
privates.threat: Silicon-carbon anodes that replace graphite threaten ALB's and MP's position in the battery materials supply chain by reducing lithium requirements per kWh and enabling denser packs that close Tesla's range advantage.

privates.name: Mariana Minerals
privates.description: Software-first vertically integrated critical minerals company using MarianaOS to autonomously operate copper and lithium mines in Utah and Texas.
privates.threat: Autonomous mining operations targeting 50,000 MT/yr copper and first GWh-scale lithium-from-produced-water facility directly threatens MP's rare earth and ALB's lithium market positions with domestically sourced supply.

privates.name: CMBlu Energy
privates.description: German non-lithium battery maker with SolidFlow organic redox technology offering 10+ hour storage without lithium, cobalt, or nickel, with supply agreements with Uniper.
privates.threat: FEOC-compliant non-lithium chemistry with 5 GWh Uniper supply agreement threatens FLNC's and EOSE's market positioning by offering a regulatory-advantaged, critical-mineral-free alternative for European grid storage.

privates.name: Stripe
privates.description: Global payments infrastructure platform processing $1.9T annually, expanding into stablecoins (Bridge), programmable wallets (Privy), and a blockchain for payments (Tempo).
privates.threat: Stripe's $1.9T payment volume and stablecoin/blockchain expansion (Bridge, Tempo) directly challenges V and MA's network fees and positions Stripe as the infrastructure layer for next-generation AI-agent-initiated payments.

privates.name: Revolut
privates.description: UK-based global neobank with 70M+ customers, full banking licenses in UK, EU, Mexico, and Australia, offering payments, crypto, insurance, and business banking.
privates.threat: Revolut's $115B valuation, full banking licenses across 4 jurisdictions, and pending US bank charter threaten PYPL's global digital wallet dominance and V/MA's cross-border fee revenue as it builds a full-stack bank.

privates.name: Ramp
privates.description: AI-powered financial operations platform for corporates covering spend management, corporate cards, procurement, accounting, and AI token spend optimization with $1B+ ARR.
privates.threat: Ramp's corporate card and AI spend management at $44B valuation competes directly with V and MA's commercial card interchange revenue and threatens PYPL's B2B push by automating the entire corporate payment workflow.

privates.name: Figure AI
privates.description: Humanoid robotics company building AI-powered general-purpose robots for commercial and residential deployment, already deployed at BMW manufacturing plants.
privates.threat: Figure's humanoid robots automating labor-intensive workflows threaten fintech-adjacent infrastructure companies like Block/XYZ that depend on human-operated retail and point-of-sale ecosystems.

privates.name: Iambic Therapeutics
privates.description: AI drug discovery company using Enchant platform for translational prediction and generative chemistry to produce clinical-stage small molecules.
privates.threat: Iambic's translational prediction platform targets the same hard-to-drug small molecule space as SDGR, potentially delivering clinical candidates faster and undercutting SDGR's commercial discovery partnerships.

privates.name: Anthropic
privates.description: AI safety company building Claude large language models with industry-leading enterprise penetration through Claude Code (coding), Cowork (agents), and API integrations.
privates.threat: Claude Code's viral adoption and Cowork agent platform threaten MSFT's GitHub Copilot monetization, CRM's Agentforce, and NOW's AI-workflow products by offering a model-layer alternative that bypasses incumbent vendor lock-in.

privates.name: OpenAI
privates.description: Developer of GPT and o-series foundation models powering ChatGPT, Codex, and enterprise APIs, with $110B raised and strategic cloud partnerships with Amazon, NVIDIA, and SoftBank.
privates.threat: OpenAI's Codex and enterprise APIs are embedding at the model layer of MSFT's Azure stack while also competing with MSFT's own Copilot products, creating internal conflicts that threaten CRM, NOW, and SNOW customer relationships.

privates.name: Databricks
privates.description: Data intelligence and AI platform (Lakehouse, Lakebase, Agent Bricks) enabling enterprises to build AI apps and agents on proprietary data, with $1.5B+ Lakebase ARR.
privates.threat: Databricks at $190B has already surpassed SNOW in private market value and its Lakebase-plus-Agent Bricks stack directly displaces SNOW's data cloud and MDB's Atlas for AI-native enterprise workloads.

privates.name: Cognition (Devin)
privates.description: Autonomous AI software engineer (Devin) with $492M ARR and 50% MoM growth serving enterprises including NASA, Goldman Sachs, and Mercedes-Benz.
privates.threat: Devin's autonomous coding with $492M ARR threatens MSFT's GitHub Copilot Enterprise pricing and CRM's developer tools by offering a full-cycle autonomous engineering agent that replaces workflow automation modules.

privates.name: Cohere
privates.description: Enterprise-focused LLM platform (Command, Embed, Rerank) built for secure, private on-premise and cloud deployments with partnerships with Oracle, SAP, Dell, and government agencies.
privates.threat: Cohere's enterprise-grade, air-gapped LLM deployment model challenges MSFT's Azure OpenAI exclusivity and GOOGL's Vertex AI by giving regulated industries (finance, defense, government) a sovereign AI option without cloud hyperscaler dependency.

privates.name: Bridge (Stripe subsidiary)
privates.description: Stablecoin orchestration platform acquired by Stripe for $1.1B, processing $400B+ in stablecoin B2B payments annually and expanding Stripe's crypto payment rails globally.
privates.threat: Bridge's $400B stablecoin volume flowing through Stripe's infrastructure threatens COIN's and CRCL's stablecoin payment ambitions by embedding crypto rails into a $159B payments incumbent that already serves 1.6% of global GDP.

privates.name: Inforcer
privates.description: MSP-focused Microsoft 365 security management platform with Shadow AI detection and real-time threat response, serving SMB clients through managed service providers.
privates.threat: Inforcer's Shadow AI detection and 300% YoY growth in the underserved SMB/MSP market threatens OKTA's identity management and CRWD's Falcon Go product by offering an all-in-one Microsoft 365 security stack at a fraction of the cost.

privates.name: Writer
privates.description: Enterprise generative AI platform for deploying AI agents across business workflows including content creation, customer support, and knowledge management with full data governance.
privates.threat: Writer's enterprise AI agent workflows with Fortune 500 customers like Vanguard and L'Oreal directly compete with CRM's Agentforce and NOW's AI workflow modules by offering model-agnostic agentic automation at lower total cost.

privates.name: Neon (Databricks subsidiary)
privates.description: Serverless Postgres database platform designed for AI agents, enabling instant spin-up of isolated database environments for agentic coding workflows (acquired by Databricks for $1B).
privates.threat: Neon's Lakebase integration into Databricks' Agent Bricks creates a purpose-built agentic database stack that threatens MDB's Atlas and SNOW's Cortex as the default data substrate for AI agent workloads.

privates.name: Klarna
privates.description: Swedish buy-now-pay-later pioneer with 85M+ consumers globally, AI-driven underwriting, and a fully automated customer service model targeting V/MA merchant fees.
privates.threat: Klarna's AI-automated underwriting and checkout network serving 85M consumers directly threatens AFRM's US market share and erodes V/MA merchant discount rates by routing BNPL transactions off traditional card rails.

events.title: Hot Chips 2026 (Aug 23-25, Stanford)
events.description: Annual IEEE symposium at Stanford (and online) covering AI accelerators, GPU architectures, packaging, and emerging silicon. Major chip companies present real-world processor and SoC designs, often used to reveal architectural details ahead of product ramps.
events.why_it_matters: First public disclosure venue for AI-chip microarchitecture details that set analyst expectations for competitive positioning in the GPU and ASIC market.

events.title: CrowdStrike Fal.Con 2026 (Aug 31 - Sep 3, Las Vegas)
events.description: CrowdStrike's flagship annual security conference at Mandalay Bay, Las Vegas, with 10,000+ attendees from 71 countries. Theme is 'Securing the AI Revolution'; CEO George Kurtz delivers keynote; 500+ sessions including platform product roadmap reveals.
events.why_it_matters: Major platform and pricing announcements at Fal.Con directly drive CRWD ARR guidance; industry buzz sets tone for cybersecurity spending entering the year-end budget cycle.

events.title: Dreamforce 2026 (Sep 15-17, San Francisco)
events.description: Salesforce's flagship global conference at the Moscone Center in San Francisco, with 1,600+ sessions and keynote by CEO Marc Benioff. Agentforce, Slack, Data 360, and Customer 360 product launches expected; streaming free on Salesforce+.
events.why_it_matters: Dreamforce is Salesforce's primary product announcement platform — Agentforce roadmap updates here directly set CRM forward bookings expectations and influence NOW/SNOW/DDOG partner ecosystems.

events.title: FDA PDUFA: Zidesamtinib (NVL-520) for ROS1 NSCLC — Sep 18
events.description: FDA target action date for zidesamtinib (NVL-520), a ROS1-inhibitor for non-small cell lung cancer. Drug developed by Nuvalent (NUVL/RPRX); not directly in universe but ZS is listed as affected on pdufa.bio by co-listing error — actual tickers per PDUFA calendar are NUVL/RPRX.
events.why_it_matters: Noted for completeness; primary impact is on NUVL and RPRX which are outside portfolio universe.

events.title: FDA PDUFA: Sotatercept (WINREVAIR) PAH expansion — NVO
events.description: FDA target action date for MRK's sotatercept-csrk (WINREVAIR) new indication for pulmonary arterial hypertension. Novo Nordisk's pipeline milestone for the same date is mim8 (denecimig) for hemophilia A with PDUFA set to September 30.
events.why_it_matters: PAH approvals redefine cardiovascular franchise value — NVO's hemophilia A approval could open a >$5B addressable market if mim8 clears FDA.

events.title: FDA PDUFA: Denecimig (Mim8) for Hemophilia A — NVO
events.description: FDA target action date for denecimig (mim8), Novo Nordisk's subcutaneous bispecific antibody for hemophilia A (with and without inhibitors). Phase 3 FRONTIER2 data published in NEJM April 2026 showed significant reduction in annualized bleeding rates versus prior prophylaxis.
events.why_it_matters: Mim8 is Novo's next major pipeline asset beyond GLP-1; a clean approval would validate NVO's diversification beyond obesity/diabetes and expand the stock's multiple.

events.title: Nasdaq-100 September 2026 Quarterly Rebalance (effective ~Sep 21)
events.description: Under Nasdaq's updated May 2026 methodology, the September quarterly review is now a formal membership checkpoint that can add/remove constituents based on full market cap ranking. TER and RKLB were added in June 2026. The September review may trigger further rotations among AI-infrastructure names.
events.why_it_matters: Under new Nasdaq-100 rules, each quarterly review can force passive-fund buying of newly added names, creating predictable demand pressure on the effective date.

events.title: FDA PDUFA: Enspryng (satralizumab) Thyroid Eye Disease — RHHBY (ABBV adjacent)
events.description: FDA target action date for Roche's satralizumab in thyroid eye disease. While ticker is RHHBY, this sets competitive context for ABBV's ophthalmology pipeline. PDUFA calendar lists October 15, 2026.
events.why_it_matters: A Roche approval in TED would intensify competition against ABBV's broader immunology portfolio and set pricing precedent.

events.title: FDA PDUFA: Bepirovirsen Hepatitis B Cure — GSK (ABBV market context)
events.description: FDA target action date for GSK's bepirovirsen for chronic hepatitis B functional cure (B-Well trial). First potential oral/injectable cure in HBV; sets competitive and market-size context for ABBV's virology assets.
events.why_it_matters: A bepirovirsen approval would validate the HBV cure market and could catalyze ABBV to accelerate its own HBV pipeline conversations with investors.

events.title: FDA PDUFA: Mitapivat (PYRUKYND) RISE UP — AGIO (ABBV royalty watch)
events.description: FDA target action date for mitapivat in sickle cell disease and thalassemia (RISE UP trial). Agios owns the drug; ABBV has royalty interests in certain hematology programs that could be affected.
events.why_it_matters: Provides data on hematology FDA review timelines relevant to broader ABBV royalty portfolio evaluation.

events.title: FDA PDUFA: Aficamten (MAPLE-HCM) — Cytokinetics (VRTX competitive context)
events.description: FDA target action date for aficamten in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy from Cytokinetics. VRTX watches this space as a potential pipeline expansion; aficamten approval would validate HCM as a large commercial market.
events.why_it_matters: Aficamten approval would intensify competition in the HCM space, setting commercial bar for VRTX's own cardiovascular pipeline.

events.title: Microsoft Ignite 2026 (Nov 17-20, San Francisco)
events.description: Microsoft's flagship annual technical conference at Moscone Center, San Francisco. CEO Satya Nadella headlines with major Azure AI, Copilot, and security product announcements. 60,000+ expected attendees; roadmap reveals for Azure OpenAI, GitHub Copilot, and enterprise AI services.
events.why_it_matters: Ignite is the primary venue for Microsoft to set enterprise AI spending expectations heading into Q4 — Azure AI services growth guidance here moves NOW and SNOW partner ARR outlook.

events.title: AWS re:Invent 2026 (Nov 30 - Dec 4, Las Vegas)
events.description: Amazon Web Services annual cloud and AI mega-conference in Las Vegas with 60,000+ attendees. 2,000+ sessions; expect launches across AWS AI services, SageMaker, Bedrock, and data platforms that compete with and partner with SNOW, DDOG, and MDB.
events.why_it_matters: AWS re:Invent drives enterprise cloud and AI procurement planning for the next year; product launches here set architectural choices that determine winners among data/observability names.

events.title: NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 Volume Ramp (Q4 2026)
events.description: NVIDIA's next-generation AI platform — Vera CPUs + Rubin GPUs in NVL72 rack configuration — enters volume production in Q4 2026 after initial Q3 shipments. Promises 5x inference performance and 10x lower cost-per-token vs. Blackwell; first adopters include OpenAI, Anthropic, and hyperscalers.
events.why_it_matters: Vera Rubin volume ramp drives NVIDIA's next revenue wave and sets Micron/SK Hynix HBM4 demand — a successful ramp accelerates all three AI-chip supply chain names.

events.title: AMD Instinct MI455X / Helios Rack Volume Shipments (Q4 2026)
events.description: AMD's Instinct MI455X (CDNA 5 architecture, 432GB HBM4, 40 PFLOPS FP4) begins volume shipping end of Q3 2026 and ramps through Q4. The Helios rack-scale solution pairs 72 MI455X GPUs for 2.9 EFLOPS of FP4 compute — AMD's direct answer to NVIDIA's NVL72.
events.why_it_matters: MI455X volume ramp is AMD's best opportunity to recapture AI datacenter share from NVIDIA; execution risk is high given supply-chain complexity at 2nm TSMC.

events.title: FDA PDUFA: Iberdomide + Daratumumab (RRMM) — BMY Aug 17
events.description: FDA target action date tomorrow (Aug 17) for Bristol-Myers Squibb's iberdomide combination in relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma. Sets competitive landscape context for ABBV's oncology/immunology pipeline.
events.why_it_matters: Iberdomide approval would validate next-generation myeloma treatment combinations, informing ABBV's partnership strategy in hematology.

events.title: FDA PDUFA: Deramiocel (CAP-1002) for Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy — CAPR Aug 22
events.description: FDA action date for Capricor's deramiocel gene therapy in Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy. Outside primary universe but illustrates near-term gene therapy regulatory environment relevant to ABBV's pipeline.
events.why_it_matters: Gene therapy FDA outcomes inform investor sentiment toward broader rare disease pipeline valuations.

events.title: FDA PDUFA: Zanidatamab (HER2+ Gastroesophageal, 1L) — Zymeworks Aug 25
events.description: FDA target action date for zanidatamab-hrii (Ziihera) in first-line HER2-positive gastroesophageal cancer. LLY and ABBV watch HER2 space for biosimilar/combination dynamics.
events.why_it_matters: Validates HER2-directed bispecific antibody market relevant to multiple large-cap biopharma pipeline overlaps.

events.title: FDA PDUFA: Bictegravir + Lenacapavir HIV Combination — GILD Aug 27
events.description: FDA target action date for Gilead's bictegravir + lenacapavir once-weekly combination for HIV. Not directly in the portfolio universe, but sets competition context for ABBV and VRTX virology programs.
events.why_it_matters: HIV regimen innovation resets long-term royalty and competitive dynamics for antiretroviral market participants.

events.title: FDA PDUFA: TLX101-Px for Glioblastoma — TELIX Sep 11
events.description: FDA target action date for Telix's TLX101-Px in recurrent/progressive glioma (brain cancer). Sets the competitive landscape for VRTX's neurology pipeline and gene therapy programs.
events.why_it_matters: Targeted radiopharmaceutical approval in hard-to-treat brain cancer validates next-generation oncology delivery modalities relevant to VRTX pipeline watch.

events.title: FDA PDUFA: Brepocitinib for Dermatomyositis — PFE/ROIV Sep 30
events.description: FDA target action date for Pfizer/Roivant's brepocitinib in dermatomyositis. VRTX's inflammatory disease pipeline overlaps with JAK inhibitor space — approval sets competitive context.
events.why_it_matters: JAK inhibitor landscape evolution in rare inflammatory diseases impacts VRTX's pipeline positioning and partnering opportunities.

events.title: FDA PDUFA: Rusfertide for Polycythemia Vera — PTGX Sep 30
events.description: FDA target action date for Protagonist Therapeutics' rusfertide (subcutaneous hepcidin mimetic) for polycythemia vera. VRTX has expressed interest in hematology adjacencies — this approval sets market context.
events.why_it_matters: Novel hematology mechanism approval signals FDA receptivity to rare blood disorder treatments adjacent to VRTX's pipeline.

events.title: FDA PDUFA: Aficamten MAPLE-HCM — CYTK Nov 14
events.description: FDA target action date for Cytokinetics' aficamten in obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Positive readout would open a $3B+ annual market and validate cardiac myosin inhibitor class.
events.why_it_matters: Aficamten approval creates direct competition for cardiac programs at LLY and would confirm HCM as priority expansion territory for both large-cap pharma and smaller biotech.

events.title: FDA PDUFA: Cemdisiran + Pozelimab (NIMBLE) — REGN Nov 30
events.description: FDA target action date for Regeneron's cemdisiran + pozelimab C5 combo in rare complement disorders. Adjacent to VRTX's rare disease ambitions and gene therapy pipeline.
events.why_it_matters: Validates complement inhibition as a durable commercial platform and signals FDA processing cadence for complex combination biologics.

events.title: FDA PDUFA: Relutrigine (PRAX-562) for Epilepsy — PRAX Dec 27
events.description: FDA target action date for Praxis' relutrigine in developmental epileptic encephalopathies. VRTX competes in rare neurological diseases and watches this space for Nav channel inhibitor activity.
events.why_it_matters: Novel sodium-channel modulator approval in DEEs would expand the rare epilepsy market and set valuation comparables for VRTX's neurology pipeline.

events.title: PJM 2028/2029 Base Residual Auction Results — Published Jul 14
events.description: PJM announced results of the 2028/2029 Base Residual Auction on July 14, 2026 — procuring 138,318 MW of UCAP generation resources. Capacity price came in at the FERC-approved cap of $325/MW-day, down 2.5%, with 6,831 MW short of the reliability requirement.
events.why_it_matters: Tight PJM capacity auction results confirm high power prices through 2028/29, supporting long-term PPA pricing and earnings visibility for CEG, VST, NRG, and TLN.

events.title: NRC Final Approval Decision: Crane Clean Energy Center (Three Mile Island Unit 1) Restart
events.description: Constellation Energy seeking final NRC license to restart the 835-MW Crane Clean Energy Center (formerly Three Mile Island Unit 1) for the Microsoft 20-year PPA. NRC has found 'no significant environmental impacts'; FERC waiver granted June 2026 enabling CIR transfer. Final approval expected late 2026/early 2027 for a 2027 commercial restart.
events.why_it_matters: NRC final approval is the last major regulatory gate before a 835 MW nuclear restart — approval validates nuclear renaissance economics and expands CEG's zero-carbon generation asset base.

events.title: Broadcom Q3 FY2026 Earnings / XPU Deployment Update (Sep 2, 2026)
events.description: Broadcom reports Q3 FY2026 results and is expected to update on its AI XPV Platform with Apollo/Blackstone ($35B initial tranche), the Jalapeño chip with OpenAI (initial deployment end-2026), and custom AI ASIC revenue guidance for hyperscalers.
events.why_it_matters: AVGO's custom ASIC (XPU) revenue from hyperscalers is the highest-margin growth driver — any upside commentary on customer pipeline or silicon volumes moves the stock significantly.

events.title: Broadcom / OpenAI Jalapeño ASIC Initial Deployment (Q4 2026)
events.description: OpenAI and Broadcom's first joint AI chip 'Jalapeño' (Intelligence Processor) targeting initial deployment by end of 2026, with prototype volumes followed by full ramp in 2027-2028. Broadcom CEO Hock Tan confirmed 'small prototype development' in late 2026.
events.why_it_matters: Jalapeño marks AVGO's strategic entry into frontier AI inference silicon — volume confirmation would validate the XPU platform thesis and add a new hyperscaler revenue stream.

events.title: TSMC CoWoS Capacity Reaches ~120-130K Wafers/Month (Q4 2026 target)
events.description: TSMC is ramping its CoWoS advanced packaging capacity from ~70-80K wafers/month (2025) toward 120-130K wafers/month by Q4 2026 — nearly doubling. All three HBM4 memory vendors (SK Hynix, Samsung, Micron) now qualified for Vera Rubin. CoWoS remains the binding bottleneck for AI hardware output with 52-78 week lead times.
events.why_it_matters: CoWoS capacity determines how fast NVIDIA and AMD can ramp AI accelerator shipments — any supply beat accelerates AI-infrastructure buildout revenue for all upstream names.

events.title: DCD Connect London 2026 (Sep 16-17)
events.description: Data Center Dynamics Connect conference in London (Sep 16-17, 2026) — major data center infrastructure event where NVIDIA, AMD, TSMC, and Broadcom customers/partners discuss capacity buildout, power requirements, and AI chip deployment timelines.
events.why_it_matters: DCD Connect is where hyperscaler infrastructure plans translate into hardware purchase announcements — supply-chain signals here move AI infrastructure names.

events.title: Pentagon 'Funding Palantir' Memo — $243.9M Through Mar 2027
events.description: Deputy Defense Secretary Steve Feinberg issued a memo on August 4, 2026 directing the Pentagon to fund up to $243.9M in Palantir services through March 31, 2027, for defense industrial base AI analytics including Maven Smart System (MSS), Gotham, and Warp Speed manufacturing OS.
events.why_it_matters: The direct Pentagon funding memo bypasses normal procurement — it accelerates PLTR's government revenue and validates DoD's dependence on Palantir's AI platforms ahead of FY2027 budget decisions.

events.title: DoD FY2027 Budget: $1.5B+ MSS Expansion Request for PLTR
events.description: Pentagon FY2027 budget materials include requests for over $1.5B to expand Palantir's Maven Smart System (MSS) across defense users supporting the 'Joint Force AI-Enabled Headquarters initiative' plus $60M for Virtual Joint Operations Center (VJOC). Congressional authorization vote expected Q4 2026.
events.why_it_matters: A $1.5B MSS expansion is an order-of-magnitude step-up from prior PLTR government contract values — congressional approval would transform PLTR's government TCV and revenue visibility.

events.title: AST SpaceMobile Reaches 13 BlueBird Satellites in Orbit
events.description: AST SpaceMobile launched BlueBirds 11, 12, and 13 on August 5, 2026 (Falcon 9 from Cape Canaveral), bringing the total BlueBird constellation to 13 satellites. Next-gen BlueBirds feature ~2,400 sq ft arrays delivering ~2x peak download speeds vs. Gen 1. Company targeting beta service in late 2026 with AT&T and Verizon.
events.why_it_matters: Each BlueBird satellite launch is a measurable step toward ASTS's revenue-generating beta service — the 13-satellite milestone positions the company for commercial launch that validates the direct-to-cell thesis.

events.title: AST SpaceMobile Beta Cellular Service Launch (Q4 2026 target)
events.description: AST SpaceMobile targeting beta cellular broadband service by end of 2026, supported by ~45 BlueBird satellites in orbit (production through satellite 42 advancing). Initial U.S. service with AT&T and Verizon will offer non-continuous coverage during the ramp phase.
events.why_it_matters: Commercial beta launch is the binary event that transforms ASTS from a development-stage company to a revenue-generating enterprise — carrier partnership validation is critical for ASTS's equity value.

events.title: AMD Advancing AI 2026: MI400 Series GPU Launch (Jul 23)
events.description: AMD officially launched the Instinct MI400 Series (MI455X + MI430X) at Advancing AI 2026 on July 23, 2026. MI455X features CDNA 5 architecture (2nm + 3nm TSMC), 432GB HBM4, 40 PFLOPS FP4, and UALoE scale-up fabric; Helios rackscale solution targets 2.9 EFLOPS of FP4 compute per rack.
events.why_it_matters: MI400 launch is AMD's strongest competitive move against NVIDIA Vera Rubin in two years — early hyperscaler adoption signals would shift market share narrative and lift MU/TSM supply chain names.

events.title: Nasdaq-100 June 2026 Rebalance: RKLB and TER Added
events.description: Nasdaq-100 added Rocket Lab (RKLB) and Teradyne (TER), along with Astera Labs, CoreWeave, and Nebius Group, effective June 22, 2026. First rebalance under new rank-based quarterly membership methodology. ZS was removed.
events.why_it_matters: Nasdaq-100 inclusion drives $800B+ of passive index fund demand in these names — the entry creates structural buying pressure around the effective date.

events.title: Nasdaq-100 December 2026 Annual Reconstitution (expected ~Dec 19)
events.description: The Nasdaq-100 annual reconstitution (third Friday of December = Dec 18, 2026, effective open Dec 19) is the primary entry point for new members. With new quarterly methodology now in place, December remains the largest rebalance. Candidates from the universe include PLTR, ASTS, and AI.
events.why_it_matters: Annual reconstitution forces the largest single-day passive fund rebalancing of the year — index inclusion can add 3-7% to affected small-cap names in the weeks before the effective date.

events.title: S&P 500 June 2026 Rebalance: Marvell Technology Added
events.description: S&P Dow Jones Indices added Marvell Technology (MRVL) to the S&P 500 effective June 22, 2026, coinciding with the quarterly rebalance. MRVL replaced Pool Corp. The addition accelerates passive fund ownership of this custom-ASIC/networking-chip designer.
events.why_it_matters: S&P 500 inclusion forces $5+ trillion in passive index AUM to buy MRVL — entry to the flagship U.S. index raises the stock's institutional ownership floor.

events.title: Snowflake Summit 2026 (June 2, San Francisco) — Key Product Updates
events.description: Snowflake Summit 2026 in San Francisco revealed the 'Agentic Enterprise' vision: Iceberg v3 interoperability, AI governance framework, new security layer, and expanded open data/AI collaboration tools. Already occurred Jun 2 — monitoring post-summit booking velocity and competitive positioning.
events.why_it_matters: Snowflake Summit product announcements set the data platform competitive landscape for H2 enterprise purchasing cycles; strong launches here validate SNOW's multi-year transition to agentic AI infrastructure.

events.title: FERC Order on PJM Backstop Capacity Auction and Data Center Curtailment
events.description: PJM board proposed backstop capacity auction and data center curtailment plans in July 2026; FERC response expected in Q3-Q4 2026. FERC's ruling 'will influence utility capital investment, data center development timelines, and the allocation of reliability risks and costs' (ClearView).
events.why_it_matters: FERC curtailment rules for data centers directly affect hyperscaler power procurement strategies and could accelerate nuclear/gas PPA demand from CEG and VST if strict limits are imposed.

events.title: GE Vernova Reaches 20 GW Annual Gas Turbine Output (Q3 2026 target)
events.description: GE Vernova is on track to deliver 20 GW of annual gas turbine output in Q3 2026, having installed 325 automated manufacturing machines with 75 more by year-end. Gas Power backlog hit 116 GW (Q2 2026); target is at least 125 GW under contract by year-end. Data center orders alone exceeded $5B YTD in 2026.
events.why_it_matters: GEV's production capacity milestone is the operational proof point that backlog will convert to revenue — achievement drives consensus estimate revisions and supports 2027 visibility.

events.title: Tesla Optimus Gen 3 Reveal + First Fremont Production Units (H2 2026)
events.description: Tesla confirmed Optimus robot production beginning at Fremont in late Q3 2026 after converting Model S/X lines; Musk warned initial output is 'quite slow' with 10,000 unique parts. Gen 3 reveal pushed to 'middle of this year' then delayed further. Volume production expectations reset; Giga Texas factory targeting summer 2027.
events.why_it_matters: Every milestone delay on Optimus erodes the 'physical AI company' valuation thesis that justifies TSLA's multiple — Gen 3 reveal quality will set consensus unit targets for 2027.

events.title: Tesla Cybercab Robotaxi Service Expansion (H2 2026)
events.description: Tesla began limited Cybercab production in Austin, Texas earlier in 2026; is expanding Tesla Robotaxi to new cities with a limited vehicle fleet. Volume production of Cybercab delayed beyond 2026 due to 4680 cell constraints. Still targeting broader commercial service launch.
events.why_it_matters: Cybercab commercial viability — not Optimus — is the more near-term autonomous revenue catalyst for TSLA; city expansion announcements are the key near-term signal.

events.title: FDA PDUFA: Atezolizumab (Tecentriq) + Stage III Colon Cancer — Roche Oct 9
events.description: FDA target action date for Roche's Tecentriq in Stage III colon cancer — competitive context for LLY's oncology pipeline including donanemab and antibody-drug conjugates.
events.why_it_matters: Colon cancer immuno-oncology approvals set reimbursement precedents and competitive framing for LLY's oncology franchise buildout.

events.title: FDA PDUFA: Ifinatamab Deruxtecan (SCLC) — MRK Oct 10
events.description: FDA target action date for Merck's ifinatamab deruxtecan (DS-7300) in extensive-stage small cell lung cancer. Sets context for LLY's antibody-drug conjugate strategy and Boehringer Ingelheim partnership.
events.why_it_matters: ADC oncology approvals in SCLC reset the treatment landscape and establish pricing/access benchmarks relevant to LLY's growing oncology pipeline.

events.title: FDA PDUFA: INO-3107 for HPV-Associated Recurrent Respiratory Papillomatosis — INOVIO Oct 30
events.description: FDA target action date for Inovio's INO-3107 DNA vaccine for HPV 6/11-associated recurrent respiratory papillomatosis. Rare disease antiviral adjacent to VRTX's immunology programs.
events.why_it_matters: First DNA vaccine FDA approval in a rare HPV indication would validate new modality and set precedent for platform-based rare disease treatments relevant to VRTX partnership watch.

events.title: FERC Order on Data Center / AI Cluster Grid Interconnection Rules (Q4 2026)
events.description: FERC is expected to issue a final rule on grid interconnection for large AI data center loads (>100 MW) in Q4 2026, following a NOI from Q2. Decision will affect how quickly hyperscalers can secure power and whether utilities must offer firm interconnection commitments.
events.why_it_matters: FERC grid rules for large AI loads directly determine the pace of new data center construction and therefore the urgency of procuring turbines (GEV), switchgear (ETN), and EPC services (PWR).

events.title: NRC License Renewal Docket: Ginna & Nine Mile Point Unit 1 Review Begins
events.description: Constellation filed license renewal applications in June 2026 to extend Ginna Clean Energy Center and Nine Mile Point Unit 1 operations to 2049. NRC docketing and initial public comment period expected to open Q3-Q4 2026.
events.why_it_matters: License renewals through 2049 create 20+ years of additional nuclear revenue visibility for CEG, reinforcing the case for nuclear PPAs at premium prices to tech companies.

events.title: All 3 HBM4 Vendors Qualified for NVIDIA Vera Rubin — Volume Shipping
events.description: As of June 2026, all three HBM4 memory vendors — SK Hynix (~62% share, volume shipping), Samsung (volume shipping after June 5 certification), and Micron (qualified, 2026 volumes fully booked) — are supplying HBM4 for NVIDIA Vera Rubin. HBM4 ramp is in progress into H2 2026.
events.why_it_matters: Multi-vendor HBM4 qualification reduces supply-chain risk for Vera Rubin ramp and increases Micron's AI HBM revenue, which is the largest upside driver in MU's fiscal 2027 guidance.

events.title: FDA PDUFA: Oveporexton (TAK-861) for Narcolepsy Type 1 — Takeda Sep 30
events.description: FDA target action date for Takeda's oveporexton in narcolepsy type 1. Validates orexin receptor agonist class which ABBV has explored in partnerships. First-in-class narcolepsy mechanism with broad commercial implications.
events.why_it_matters: Narcolepsy orexin agonist approval would unlock a $3B+ annual market and validate a novel CNS mechanism relevant to ABBV's neuroscience pipeline strategy.

events.title: FDA PDUFA: Ameluz (ALA HCl) for Basal Cell Carcinoma — Sep 28
events.description: FDA target action date for Biofrontera's aminolevulinic acid hydrochloride photodynamic therapy in basal cell carcinoma. Sets context for dermatology-oncology intersection relevant to VRTX's MRGPRX2 and other dermatology programs.
events.why_it_matters: BCC is a high-prevalence skin cancer; photodynamic therapy approval sets reimbursement context relevant to VRTX's dermatology expansion plans.

events.title: Eli Lilly Foundayo (Orforglipron) Launch — Commercial Ramp Begins
events.description: FDA approved LLY's orforglipron (Foundayo) for obesity on April 1, 2026 — the first oral GLP-1 pill for weight loss without food/water restrictions, available via LillyDirect starting at $25/month with coverage. Commercial ramp underway through H2 2026.
events.why_it_matters: Oral GLP-1 significantly expands the addressable market for obesity treatment by removing the injection barrier — LLY commercial uptake data in H2 2026 will set the street's 2027 obesity revenue model.

events.title: FDA PDUFA: Leniolisib for PI3K-delta Syndrome — PHAR Oct 24
events.description: FDA target action date for Pharming Group's leniolisib in activated PI3K-delta syndrome — rare primary immunodeficiency. VRTX's rare disease strategy includes potential immunodeficiency programs and gene therapy collaborations.
events.why_it_matters: PI3K-delta rare disease approval validates targeted immunology mechanisms and sets rare disease pricing precedents relevant to VRTX's portfolio expansion.

events.title: Rocket Lab Neutron Rocket: Development Milestone Update (Q4 2026)
events.description: Rocket Lab's medium-lift Neutron rocket is in development for first launch targeting 2026-2027. RKLB added to Nasdaq-100 in June 2026 on strong Electron cadence and Neutron progress. Structural test articles and propulsion testing milestones expected in H2 2026.
events.why_it_matters: Neutron program milestones are the primary catalyst for RKLB's medium-launch market entry — any schedule confirmation or propulsion success would materially re-rate the stock's addressable market valuation.

events.title: AWS re:Invent 2026 Final Days (Dec 4) + December Index Rebalance Window
events.description: AWS re:Invent runs Nov 30 - Dec 4, 2026. The December 2026 window also includes the Nasdaq-100 annual reconstitution (effective ~Dec 19), S&P 500 December rebalance, and year-end portfolio positioning. Cloud and AI infrastructure spending announcements from re:Invent will inform Q4 bookings.
events.why_it_matters: December is the highest-stakes period for enterprise software and cloud names — re:Invent announcements and index reconstitution together create the largest simultaneous buying pressure of the year.

events.title: Datacloud USA 2026 (Sep 2-4, Austin TX)
events.description: Industry data center and cloud conference in Austin, September 2-4, 2026. Infrastructure and software vendors present data sovereignty, AI workload optimization, and hybrid cloud architectures.
events.why_it_matters: Enterprise data platform conversations at Datacloud USA set H2 procurement priorities for the names competing in AI data infrastructure.

events.title: IRA Energy Storage Tax Credit Guidance: Treasury Final Rules (Expected Q4 2026)
events.description: U.S. Treasury expected to issue final rules clarifying the Inflation Reduction Act Section 48E investment tax credits for standalone energy storage and Section 45X advanced manufacturing credits in Q4 2026. Affects ENPH, FSLR, FLNC, EOSE financial models.
events.why_it_matters: IRA ITC guidance clarity removes a major uncertainty for storage project financing — positive finalization would unlock project investment decisions that drive FLNC and EOSE revenue backlogs.

events.title: DoD Critical Minerals Supply Chain — MP Materials Production Milestone
events.description: MP Materials is ramping rare earth magnet production at its Fort Worth, Texas facility under a DoD-backed offtake agreement with GM. Q4 2026 production targets for neodymium-iron-boron magnet output are the key financial milestone. Additional DoD contract awards for domestic rare earth supply expected.
events.why_it_matters: MP's magnet production ramp converts rare earth processing into vertically integrated revenue — DoD contract expansions reduce single-customer risk and establish long-term price floors.

events.title: Albemarle Lithium Pricing Cycle: Q4 Contract Resets
events.description: Albemarle (ALB) has annual/quarterly lithium contract reset periods — Q4 2026 pricing negotiations for 2027 supply contracts will set ALB's revenue trajectory. Global lithium spot prices and Chinese supply dynamics determine contract terms.
events.why_it_matters: ALB's earnings leverage is almost entirely lithium price-driven — Q4 contract resets above current low spot prices would be the single largest catalyst for ALB's 2027 guidance uplift.

events.title: SEC Digital Asset Regulatory Clarity — Ongoing Rulemaking (H2 2026)
events.description: SEC and CFTC joint digital asset rulemaking framework expected to clarify crypto securities definitions and exchange registration requirements in H2 2026 following Congressional legislation in Q1 2026. COIN and HOOD have significant exposure to regulatory certainty.
events.why_it_matters: SEC final digital asset rules would remove the single largest regulatory overhang on COIN — clarity on crypto classification directly unlocks institutional product expansion and IPO pipeline access.

events.title: DoD FY2027 Authorization Act — NDAA Signing (Expected Dec 2026)
events.description: The National Defense Authorization Act for FY2027 is expected to be signed in December 2026. Key provisions relevant to portfolio: AI/autonomous systems procurement (PLTR Maven, KTOS attritable drones, AVAV small UAS), hypersonic program funding (LMT, RTX), and space systems spending (LHX, LDOS).
events.why_it_matters: NDAA sets multi-year defense spending authorization — above-consensus autonomous systems and AI budget lines directly translate into LTM contract award pipelines for all defense names.

events.title: NASA CLPS Lunar Surface Mission — Intuitive Machines / Firefly Award Update
events.description: NASA's Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS) program has ongoing task order awards through Q4 2026. Intuitive Machines (LUNR) is executing on IM-2 and preparing IM-3 — any new CLPS task order awards or launch date confirmations are significant catalysts.
events.why_it_matters: LUNR's entire near-term revenue is CLPS-dependent — contract wins and launch schedule confirmations directly drive backlog and cash burn trajectory.

events.title: CrowdStrike CrowdTour (Oct 8+) — Regional Cybersecurity Summits
events.description: Following Fal.Con 2026 (Aug 31-Sep 3), CrowdStrike launches CrowdTour regional summits starting October 8, 2026, across major cities. Partner-facing summits drive pipeline and partner revenue metrics for Q4.
events.why_it_matters: CrowdTour pipeline events in October directly feed Q4 bookings acceleration for CRWD's fiscal Q4 (Jan) — partner-generated ARR is the fastest-growing ARR segment.

events.title: NEJM / Cell Symposia on AI Drug Discovery — Q4 2026 Academic Conferences
events.description: Multiple Q4 2026 academic symposia (ASH, ASCO Winter, AACR) will feature clinical and computational data from RXRX, SDGR, and TEM AI-designed drug programs. ASH (American Society of Hematology) annual meeting expected December 4-7, 2026.
events.why_it_matters: ASH and other Q4 medical meetings are where AI drug-discovery pipeline data gets its first public scientific validation — positive clinical data at ASH drives rerating of RXRX/SDGR platform valuations.

ipos.name: Cerebras Systems
ipos.description: Designer of the Wafer-Scale Engine 3 AI inference chip and cloud-based AI compute service; counts OpenAI and AWS as customers.
ipos.read_across: A $56B Cerebras listing establishes a pure-play AI-inference comp that pressures NVDA's monopoly narrative and validates AMD's rival inference ambitions.

ipos.name: SpaceX
ipos.description: Vertically integrated rocket, Starlink satellite internet, and xAI division — the largest IPO ever by gross proceeds.
ipos.read_across: A $1.77T SpaceX listing instantly revalues ASTS, RKLB, and LUNR as small-cap proxies while compressing satellite-broadband TAM for DISH and legacy telecoms.

ipos.name: X-energy
ipos.description: Developer of the Xe-100 small modular reactor and TRISO nuclear fuel; backed by Amazon, Dow, and Jane Street for 5+ GW of contracted power.
ipos.read_across: X-energy's SMR premium re-rates OKLO and NuScale on a technology-licensing model, and signals that hyperscalers will pay through-the-cycle offtake prices for 24/7 carbon-free power.

ipos.name: Fervo Energy
ipos.description: Advanced geothermal energy developer supplying baseload, carbon-free electricity to data centers; backed by Breakthrough Energy Ventures and Devon Energy.
ipos.read_across: Fervo's $10B debut validates next-gen geothermal as a credible grid asset, pressuring NEE and AES to accelerate geothermal M&A to protect their power-to-datacenter pipelines.

ipos.name: Generate Biomedicines
ipos.description: Clinical-stage generative biology company using AI to design proteins and drug molecules for previously undruggable targets.
ipos.read_across: GENB's listing gives the market a pure-play generative-biology comp that re-rates RXRX and SEER on AI-designed drug probability of success, while pressuring Genentech to defend its structure-based design moat.

ipos.name: Lyntris
ipos.description: Defense technology company delivering sense-to-act connectivity for multi-domain battlespace; formed by merger of Accelerint and Vitesse Systems.
ipos.read_across: Lyntris's NYSE debut expands the investable defense-autonomy comp set, directly re-rating L3Harris and CACI on battlespace connectivity multiples.

ipos.name: Syntiant
ipos.description: Ultra-low-power AI processor and full-stack physical AI platform for always-on edge intelligence in audio, vision, and sensor applications.
ipos.read_across: A Syntiant listing prices always-on edge-AI silicon as a discrete category, putting MCHP and QCOM's embedded-AI ambitions under multiple pressure if edge inference proves margin-rich.

ipos.name: Csquare
ipos.description: Carrier-neutral data center colocation and interconnection platform across US, Canada, and UK, serving AI-enabled cloud workloads.
ipos.read_across: Csquare's NYSE listing benchmarks private colocation multiples against EQIX and DLR, compressing or expanding their premiums depending on whether Csquare prices AI-capacity scarcity into rents.

ipos.name: Anthropic
ipos.description: Creator of the Claude family of AI models and Claude Code agentic coding assistant; revenue run rate of $47B as of mid-2026.
ipos.read_across: An Anthropic listing near $1T sets a forward-revenue multiple for the AI-model layer that forces MSFT and GOOG to justify their AI capex-to-revenue ratios in real time.

ipos.name: OpenAI
ipos.description: Creator of ChatGPT and GPT-4o with 900M+ weekly active users; confidential S-1 filed June 2026 after structural conversion from nonprofit.
ipos.read_across: An OpenAI public listing would be the defining valuation benchmark for the entire AI software stack, immediately repricing MSFT's Azure-OpenAI revenue share and Google's Gemini monetization argument.

ipos.name: Spin AI
ipos.description: AI-driven SaaS security and data-protection platform for enterprise cloud applications, guarding against ransomware, shadow AI, and data exposure.
ipos.read_across: Spin AI's listing creates a pure-play SaaS-security comp that forces CrowdStrike and Zscaler to demonstrate they can replicate behavioral SaaS monitoring at platform margins.

ipos.name: HawkEye 360
ipos.description: Radio frequency intelligence company using a commercial satellite constellation to detect, characterize, and geolocate RF signals for military customers.
ipos.read_across: HawkEye 360's NYSE filing re-rates ASTS and Palantir's geospatial-intelligence business as pure spectrum-surveillance comparables surge on defense-budget tailwinds.

ipos.name: Anduril Industries
ipos.description: Defense autonomy company making AI-powered drones, missiles, and Lattice OS for the US military; $2.2B 2025 revenue; $100B valuation talks in July 2026.
ipos.read_across: An Anduril IPO near $100B would directly re-rate Lockheed Martin and Northrop Grumman as incumbents fighting for vertical-integration relevance against a software-native defense prime.

ipos.name: Shield AI
ipos.description: Autonomous flight software (Hivemind) and V-BAT UAV maker; selected by USAF for CCA Collaborative Combat Aircraft program; $540M+ projected 2026 revenue.
ipos.read_across: A Shield AI public listing benchmarks autonomy-software multiples against Palantir's 60x forward revenue, compelling L3Harris and Textron to pay up for any remaining autonomy M&A targets.

ipos.name: Unitree Robotics
ipos.description: China's leading humanoid robot manufacturer (G1 model); first humanoid to list on Shanghai's STAR market; backed by DeepSeek and Chinese government funds.
ipos.read_across: A $9B Unitree STAR listing raises the valuation bar for all humanoid-robot manufacturers and forces Tesla's Optimus and Figure AI to match aggressive Chinese cost curves in investor presentations.

ipos.name: Databricks
ipos.description: Data lakehouse and AI platform with $7B+ revenue run rate and 80%+ YoY growth; raised $5B at $190B in August 2026; IPO repeatedly deferred.
ipos.read_across: Any Databricks IPO announcement would force Snowflake to defend its data-warehouse multiple against a larger, faster-growing AI-native platform trading at a premium.

ipos.name: Yellow.ai
ipos.description: Enterprise agentic AI platform for service automation with 16B conversations/year across 650+ enterprise clients; going public via SPAC merger with Bluerock Acquisition Corp.
ipos.read_across: Yellow.ai's SPAC listing tests whether agentic-AI-for-CX can command SaaS multiples, directly pressuring Five9 and NICE inContact on AI-displacement narrative.

ipos.name: GrubMarket
ipos.description: AI-powered food supply chain platform with $2B+ revenue and GrubAssist AI suite for wholesalers and distributors; confidential S-1 filed July 2026.
ipos.read_across: GrubMarket's IPO reprices vertical-SaaS-plus-marketplace hybrids in agriculture, giving AGCO and Corteva a software-valuation comp that highlights the hardware discount in legacy agri companies.

ipos.name: Kailera Therapeutics
ipos.description: Developer of oral and injectable treatments for obesity and metabolic disease, advancing next-generation GLP-1 receptor agonists.
ipos.read_across: Kailera's $718M raise reinforces the GLP-1 obesity-drug mega-cycle and re-rates Viking Therapeutics and Structure Therapeutics as next-wave acqui-hire targets for Eli Lilly and Novo Nordisk.

ipos.name: Alamar Biosciences
ipos.description: Applies proteomics and AI to early disease detection; ultra-sensitive protein biomarker platform targeting liquid biopsy and multi-cancer early detection.
ipos.read_across: Alamar's proteomics listing competes directly with Seer and Olink for liquid-biopsy multiple, forcing Illumina to defend its genomics dominance narrative against protein-first diagnostics.

ipos.name: Applied Aerospace and Defense
ipos.description: Huntsville, AL-based supplier of propellant tanks, antennas, engine nozzles, and payload adapters for defense and space missions; $500M 2025 revenue.
ipos.read_across: Applied Aerospace's NYSE listing creates a component-supply comp that pressures Moog and Heico on space-hardware margins as commercial launch cadence accelerates.

ipos.name: American Battery Materials
ipos.description: Exploration-stage US critical minerals company developing direct lithium extraction from Utah's Paradox Basin brine deposits; NYSE American uplisting.
ipos.read_across: BLTH's NYSE uplisting highlights the domestic critical-minerals investment gap and re-rates ALB and SQM on US lithium supply security arguments favored by IRA-era policy.

ipos.name: Seaport Therapeutics
ipos.description: Boston biotech developing psychedelic-inspired and neurosteroid medicines for depression, anxiety, and neuropsychiatric disorders using proprietary delivery science.
ipos.read_across: Seaport's listing prices the CNS-neuropsychiatric pipeline against AbbVie's Cerevel acquisition and forces AXSM and INVA to defend their depression drug multiples against next-gen mechanisms.

ipos.name: Hemab
ipos.description: Denmark-based biotech developing treatments for rare blood coagulation disorders, including thrombomodulin-based agents for hemophilia.
ipos.read_across: Hemab's Nasdaq listing re-rates Sanofi-Genzyme's hemophilia franchise and forces BioMarin to price next-generation coagulation mechanisms into its pipeline value.

ipos.name: Saronic
ipos.description: Builder of autonomous maritime vessels for US Navy and USCG missions; raised significant 2026 funding amid defense-autonomy boom.
ipos.read_across: A Saronic IPO creates the first pure-play autonomous surface vessel comp, directly pressuring HII and Austal on traditional naval shipbuilding margins as the Navy shifts to autonomous surface fleets.

ipos.name: AgiBot
ipos.description: Chinese humanoid robot manufacturer competing with Unitree; seeking IPO listing in Hong Kong following Unitree's successful STAR market debut.
ipos.read_across: AgiBot's HK listing extends the humanoid-robot public comp set and forces Boston Dynamics parent Hyundai to acknowledge the valuation gap between private-market enthusiasm and revenue reality.

ipos.name: Klarna
ipos.description: Swedish BNPL and AI-powered payments platform with 150M+ consumers; repeatedly named in credible 2026 US IPO reporting alongside Stripe.
ipos.read_across: Klarna's US IPO would directly reprice AFRM and SoFi on BNPL economics while signaling whether European fintech can achieve US growth-stock multiples on a Nasdaq listing.

ipos.name: Razorpay
ipos.description: India's leading payments and fintech infrastructure company; filed pre-DRHP with SEBI seeking $500-600M in a domestic Indian IPO.
ipos.read_across: Razorpay's SEBI filing prices India's payments infrastructure at a premium that compresses Paytm's discount while signaling to VISA and Mastercard that domestic Indian rails may commoditize cross-border margins.

ipos.name: Leju Robotics
ipos.description: Chinese humanoid robot company seeking listing on Shenzhen exchange; part of the wave of Chinese humanoid manufacturers racing to public markets post-Unitree.
ipos.read_across: Leju's Shenzhen listing deepens the humanoid-robot investable universe, intensifying valuation scrutiny on Boston Dynamics and NVIDIA's Isaac robotics platform as pure-play comps multiply.

ipos.name: Mobia Medical
ipos.description: Austin-based developer of a nerve-stimulation device for stroke recovery; filed S-1 in April 2026 targeting rehab neurology market.
ipos.read_across: Mobia's listing benchmarks non-invasive neuromodulation against Nevro and Nalu Medical, giving MDVN and Abbott a read on how the market prices clinical-stage neurostimulation absent insurance reimbursement clarity.

ipos.name: Swarmer
ipos.description: Defense drone swarming company that had a soaring public debut in 2026, referenced as an early marker for defense-tech IPO appetite.
ipos.read_across: Swarmer's pop set the benchmark for autonomous-drone multiples and validated investor willingness to price software-defined munitions at premiums over legacy defense hardware primes.

ipos.name: LimX Dynamics
ipos.description: Chinese robotics company building bipedal and quadruped robots; founder stated publicly that 'listing is a must' following Unitree's successful debut.
ipos.read_across: LimX's IPO intent extends the Chinese humanoid comp wave and puts pressure on US robotics developers to accelerate commercialization timelines before the cost-curve gap with Chinese manufacturers widens further.

Institutional aggregate signals (e.g. '48% net buyers of semis') are from a Reuters analysis of 6,371 filers. Dollar values and share counts for Tiger Global and Coatue are sourced from danielscrivner.com which cites the SEC 13F; Bridgewater and Viking from last10k.com which parses SEC filings; Appaloosa from particle.news, newsquawk.com, and Yahoo Finance, all citing SEC filings.
